decisions.choice: oracle: a solemn pronouncement from God
decisions.reason: The word heads prophetic messages, especially messages of judgment (Isaiah 13:1; Nahum 1:1; Malachi 1:1). Here it introduces a book that begins with the prophet's own complaint to God, God's answer and a prayer; the whole is the message God gave him (see the note at Isaiah 13:1).

decisions.choice: Habakkuk the prophet: a prophet in the last years of Judah
decisions.reason: Nothing is known of Habakkuk beyond this book; the meaning of his name is uncertain. The book speaks of the Chaldeans, the Babylonians, as about to rise to power (1:6). That points to the last decades before Babylon took Jerusalem, around the time Nebuchadnezzar defeated Egypt at Carchemish (605 BC). Habakkuk is one of the few prophets called "the prophet" in the heading of his book, as Haggai and Zechariah are.

decisions.choice: saw: received in a vision
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for a prophet's vision (Isaiah 1:1; Amos 1:1). What the prophet "saw" was a message from God, and God tells him to write "the vision" in 2:2.

decisions.choice: message; received in a vision
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah and Nahum, Readable says "message" for "oracle" and explains "saw".

decisions.choice: "L'oracle" (L, B); "le message" (R), for *massa*, in Habakkuk, Zephaniah, Haggai and Zechariah
decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording for *massa* as a title ("Oracle sur …" / "Message au sujet de …"), here without a named nation; Readable says what the English Readable says, a message received in a vision.

decisions.choice: The prophets' words, complaints and God's answers are speech: present, future and passé composé at every level, never passé simple; the past in Habakkuk 3 is in the passé composé, as the Psalms. Narrative frames (Haggai's dated reports, Zechariah's visions told in the first person) take the passé simple at L and B and the passé composé at R
alternatives: passé simple for past events at L and B throughout
decisions.reason: As the term sheet for Lamentations, Ezekiel, Daniel and the Twelve: oracles and prayers are spoken, not written narration. The heading keeps "vit" at L and B, as Isaiah 13:1.

decisions.choice: "oráculo" (L, B); "mensaje ... recibió en una visión" (R)
decisions.reason: Massa is "oráculo" at L and B and "mensaje" at R, as in the Spanish Isaiah and the rest of the Twelve; this choice holds through Habakkuk, Zephaniah, Haggai and Zechariah. "Vio" is kept at L and B; R says the seeing was a vision, as the English R does.

decisions.choice: "Habacuc"
decisions.reason: The usual Spanish form of the prophet's name.

decisions.choice: "Unabii" (L, B); "ujumbe" (R)
decisions.reason: The oracle (massa') is worded as in Isaiah 13:1 and the term sheet for the Twelve. The prophet's name is "Habakuki" in this book and in its later headings. Recorded once for Habakkuk, Zephaniah, Haggai and Zechariah 1-4.

decisions.choice: "aliuona" (L, B); "aliupokea katika maono" (R)
decisions.reason: "Saw" is kept at L and B, as Isaiah 13:1; Readable says plainly that the message came in a vision, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: *massa'* is "신탁" (L, B) and "말씀" (R), as in Isaiah; "예언자 하박국"
decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording for *massa'* (Isaiah 13:1; 2 Kings 9:25). Habakkuk is spelled as published ("하박국"); the prophet is "예언자", the modern word the style guide prefers to "선지자".

decisions.choice: "Sấm ngôn" (L, B) / "sứ điệp" (R) for massa'
decisions.reason: The terms note for massa' in Habakkuk, as in Isaiah and Nahum. Book-wide choices for this job (Habakkuk, Zephaniah, Haggai, Zechariah 1-4), recorded once here: CHÚA is the divine-name span at every level; "the Lord GOD" is "Chúa là CHÚA"; "the LORD of hosts" is "CHÚA Vạn Quân" with the span on CHÚA only; God's oracles take no quotation marks; the prophet calls himself "con" and God "Ngài" or "Chúa" when he prays, with "lạy CHÚA" for the vocative; God says "các ngươi" to the people in rebuke; the Chaldeans are "người Canh-đê" (L, B) / "người Ba-by-lôn" (R).

decisions.choice: "nhận được qua khải tượng" for "saw"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision: he saw it in a vision; Readable says so, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: O oráculo (L); A mensagem (B, R); Habacuque, o profeta (L); o profeta Habacuque (B, R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: massa' is "oráculo" at Literal and "mensagem" at Balanced and Readable, the wording Isaiah 13:1 and Nahum 1:1 set in Portuguese, although the English Balanced keeps "oracle" here. The prophet's name takes its usual Portuguese form, "Habacuque".

source.text: עַד־אָ֧נָה יְהוָ֛ה שִׁוַּ֖עְתִּי וְלֹ֣א תִשְׁמָ֑ע אֶזְעַ֥ק אֵלֶ֛יךָ חָמָ֖ס וְלֹ֥א תוֹשִֽׁיעַ׃

records.literal_gloss: Until when, Yahweh, have I cried for help, and you do not hear? I cry out to you, Violence! and you do not save.

en.L: How long, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, have I cried for help, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do not hear? \q I cry out to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, "Violence!" and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do not save.
en.B: How long, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, must I cry for help while {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do not listen? \q I cry out to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, "Violence!" but {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do not save.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, how long must I call to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} for help before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} listen? \q I cry out to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} that violence is everywhere, but {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do not rescue us.

fr.L: Jusqu’à quand, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, ai-je crié au secours, et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} n’entends pas ? \q Je crie vers {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} : « Violence ! » et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ne sauves pas.
fr.B: Jusqu’à quand, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, devrai-je appeler au secours sans que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} écoutes ? \q Je crie vers {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} : « Violence ! » mais {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ne sauves pas.
fr.R: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, combien de temps vais-je encore {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} supplier de m’aider avant que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} m’écoutes ? \q Je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} crie que la violence est partout, mais {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ne nous délivres pas.

es.L: ¿Hasta cuándo, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, he clamado pidiendo auxilio, y no escuchas? \q Clamo a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}: «¡Violencia!», y no salvas.
es.B: ¿Hasta cuándo, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, tendré que pedir ayuda sin que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} me escuches? \q Clamo a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}: «¡Violencia!», pero no salvas.
es.R: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, ¿hasta cuándo tendré que clamar a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} pidiendo ayuda sin que me escuches? \q Te grito que hay violencia por todas partes, pero no nos rescatas.

sw.L: Hadi lini, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nimelia kuomba msaada, {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}} husikii? \q Ninakulilia, "Dhuluma!" {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}} huokoi.
sw.B: Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nitalia kuomba msaada hadi lini, {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}} husikilizi? \q Ninakulilia, "Dhuluma!" lakini huokoi.
sw.R: Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nitakuita kuomba msaada hadi lini kabla hujanisikiliza? \q Ninakulilia kwamba dhuluma iko kila mahali, lakini hutuokoi.

vi.L: Cho đến bao giờ, lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, con kêu cứu mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không nghe? \q Con kêu lên với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Bạo lực!" mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không giải cứu.
vi.B: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, con phải kêu cứu đến bao giờ mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vẫn không lắng nghe? \q Con kêu lên với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Bạo lực!" nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chẳng ra tay cứu.
vi.R: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, con phải kêu xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} giúp đỡ đến bao lâu nữa thì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mới nghe? \q Con kêu lên với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} rằng bạo lực ở khắp nơi, nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không giải cứu chúng con.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 언제까지 제가 도와 달라고 부르짖어야 하며, 주님께서는 듣지 않으십니까? \q 제가 주님께 "폭력이다!" 하고 외쳐도 주님께서는 구원하지 않으십니다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 언제까지 제가 도와 달라고 부르짖어야 합니까? 주님께서는 들어 주지 않으십니다. \q 제가 주님께 "폭력이다!" 하고 외쳐도 주님께서는 구해 주지 않으십니다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 제가 언제까지 주님께 도와 달라고 외쳐야 주님께서 들어 주시겠습니까? \q 사방에 폭력이 가득하다고 제가 주님께 부르짖어도, 주님께서는 저희를 구해 주지 않으십니다.

pt.L: Até quando, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, clamarei por socorro, e {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} não ouvirás? \q Grito a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}: "Violência!", e {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} não salvas.
pt.B: Até quando, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, terei de pedir socorro sem que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} escutes? \q Clamo a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}: "Violência!", mas {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} não salvas.
pt.R: {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, até quando vou ter de chamar por {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} pedindo ajuda, até que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} me escutes? \q Grito a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} que há violência por toda parte, mas {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} não nos livras.

decisions.choice: How long, LORD?: the prophet's complaint to God
decisions.reason: The book opens not with God's word to the people but with the prophet's words to God. "How long?" is the cry of the lament psalms (Psalm 13:2-3; 74:10). Habakkuk complains in 1:2-4, the LORD answers in 1:5-11, Habakkuk complains again in 1:12-2:1, and the LORD answers in 2:2-20.

decisions.choice: Violence!: the cry of someone being wronged
decisions.reason: The word means violent wrongdoing: brutality, oppression, the crushing of the weak (Genesis 6:11; Jeremiah 6:7). Crying "Violence!" was a call for help, like crying "Help!" or "Murder!" (Job 19:7; Jeremiah 20:8). Verses 3-4 show that the violence is within Judah itself.

decisions.choice: that violence is everywhere; rescue us
decisions.reason: Readable makes the cry part of the sentence and adds "us", the people who suffer the violence.

decisions.choice: "¿Hasta cuándo, SEÑOR ...?" with "tú" for God
decisions.reason: The prophet speaks to God with "tú", as the term sheet sets for Habakkuk 1 and 3; the vocative takes no "oh". God's pronouns are written as free words ("a ti", "tú") so that they can carry the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: Habakkuk speaks to God in 합쇼체 with "저" and "주님", and the vocative is "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}여"; God answers in 해라체 with "나" and "너희". No deity_pronoun spans
decisions.reason: The term sheet's address forms: the prophets' complaints are 합쇼체 and God speaks 해라체, naming himself without -시-. Korean has no capital letters, so the English deity_pronoun spans have nothing to change; respect is carried by -시- and "주님". Recorded once for Habakkuk, Zephaniah, Haggai and Zechariah 1–4.

decisions.choice: the prophet calls himself "con" and God "Ngài"
decisions.reason: The terms note: a prophet speaking to God says "con" and calls him "Ngài" (spanned mid-sentence); "lạy CHÚA" for the vocative, with no "O".

decisions.choice: "Ee BWANA" as the vocative, with the divine_name span on BWANA
decisions.reason: Swahili addresses God with the vocative "Ee", as the published Psalms and the Isaiah and Jeremiah blocks do. Recorded once for this job.

decisions.choice: "Dhuluma!"
decisions.reason: Chamas is wrong done to someone; "dhuluma" (oppression, injustice) is the cry of a person wronged, which the meaning decision describes. "Ukatili" would stress cruelty only.

decisions.choice: spans only on free pronouns and possessives that mean God, mid-sentence ("nami", "naye", "mimi", "kwangu", "wangu", "yake"), never on verb prefixes
alternatives: a span on every pronoun, as in English
decisions.reason: Swahili marks most pronouns for God inside the verb ("husikii", "huokoi"), and a verb prefix or object marker cannot take a capital, so the deity_pronoun span stands only on free pronouns and possessives. Habakkuk therefore has fewer spans in Swahili than in English. Mid-sentence, every free pronoun or possessive that means God takes the span, including "mimi", "nami", "naye", "yeye" and "kwangu", even where the English has none; a word that opens a sentence is written plainly with its capital, and "naye" followed by a noun ("naye BWANA") is a conjunction with no span. This holds for the whole book, as in Ezekiel and the rest of the Twelve.

decisions.choice: Até quando, SENHOR (L, B); tu, ti, teu for the prophet speaking to God, with deity_pronoun spans
decisions.reason: For the whole book: Habakkuk speaks to God with "tu", as the psalms of lament do (m1), and the opening cry takes the words of Psalm 13:2 in Portuguese, "Até quando, SENHOR". Where Portuguese drops a subject pronoun there is no span; where it keeps one for clarity or emphasis ("e tu não salvas"), it takes the span, as the English "you" does.

source.text: לָ֣מָּה תַרְאֵ֤נִי אָ֨וֶן֙ וְעָמָ֣ל תַּבִּ֔יט וְשֹׁ֥ד וְחָמָ֖ס לְנֶגְדִּ֑י וַיְהִ֧י רִ֦יב וּמָד֖וֹן יִשָּֽׂא׃

records.literal_gloss: Why do you make me see iniquity, and trouble do you look at? And destruction and violence [are] before me; and there is strife, and contention arises.

en.L: Why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} make me see iniquity, and [why] do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} look on trouble? \q Destruction and violence [are] before me; \q there is strife, and contention arises.
en.B: Why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} make me see wrongdoing? Why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} put up with trouble? \q Ruin and violence are in front of me; \q quarrels and conflict break out.
en.R: Why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} make me watch people do evil? Why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} just look on while they cause trouble? \q Everywhere I look there is destruction and violence. \q People argue and fight.

fr.L: Pourquoi me fais-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} voir l’iniquité, et [pourquoi] regardes-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} la peine ? \q Dévastation et violence [sont] devant moi ; \q il y a querelle, et la discorde s’élève.
fr.B: Pourquoi me fais-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} voir le mal ? Pourquoi tolères-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} la misère ? \q Le ravage et la violence sont sous mes yeux ; \q les querelles et les conflits éclatent.
fr.R: Pourquoi me fais-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} voir des gens faire le mal ? Pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} contentes-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} de regarder pendant qu’ils causent du malheur ? \q Partout où je regarde, il y a destruction et violence. \q Les gens se disputent et se battent.

es.L: ¿Por qué me haces ver iniquidad, y [por qué] miras el sufrimiento? \q Destrucción y violencia [hay] delante de mí; \q hay contienda, y se levanta discordia.
es.B: ¿Por qué me haces ver la maldad? ¿Por qué toleras la opresión? \q Ruina y violencia están delante de mí; \q surgen pleitos y contiendas.
es.R: ¿Por qué me haces ver cómo la gente hace el mal? ¿Por qué solo miras mientras causan sufrimiento? \q Dondequiera que miro hay destrucción y violencia. \q La gente discute y pelea.

sw.L: Kwa nini unanifanya nione uovu, na [kwa nini] unatazama taabu? \q Uharibifu na dhuluma [viko] mbele yangu; \q kuna ugomvi, na mabishano yanainuka.
sw.B: Kwa nini unanionyesha maovu? Kwa nini unavumilia taabu? \q Uharibifu na dhuluma viko mbele yangu; \q magomvi na mabishano yanazuka.
sw.R: Kwa nini unanifanya niwatazame watu wakitenda maovu? Kwa nini unatazama tu wanaposababisha taabu? \q Kila ninapotazama kuna uharibifu na dhuluma. \q Watu wanabishana na kupigana.

vi.L: Tại sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bắt con thấy sự gian ác, và [tại sao] {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nhìn xem điều khổ nạn? \q Sự tàn phá và bạo lực [ở] trước mặt con; \q có tranh chấp, và cãi vã nổi lên.
vi.B: Tại sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bắt con chứng kiến điều sai trái? Tại sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cứ dung thứ cảnh khổ đau? \q Tàn phá và bạo lực ở ngay trước mắt con; \q tranh chấp và xung đột nổi lên khắp nơi.
vi.R: Tại sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bắt con phải nhìn người ta làm điều ác? Tại sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chỉ đứng nhìn khi họ gây khổ cho người khác? \q Nhìn đâu con cũng thấy tàn phá và bạo lực. \q Người ta cãi cọ và đánh nhau.

ko.L: 어찌하여 주님께서는 저에게 죄악을 보게 하시며, 고통을 바라보기만 하십니까? \q 파멸과 폭력이 제 앞에 [있고], \q 다툼이 있고 싸움이 일어납니다.
ko.B: 어찌하여 주님께서는 저에게 악한 일을 보게 하십니까? 어찌하여 고통을 그냥 두고 보십니까? \q 파괴와 폭력이 제 눈앞에 있고, \q 다툼과 싸움이 끊이지 않습니다.
ko.R: 왜 주님께서는 사람들이 악한 짓을 하는 것을 제가 보게 하십니까? 왜 그들이 괴롭히는 것을 보고만 계십니까? \q 어디를 보아도 부서지고 짓밟히는 일뿐입니다. \q 사람들이 서로 말다툼하고 싸웁니다.

pt.L: Por que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} me fazes ver a iniquidade, e [por que] olhas para a aflição? \q Destruição e violência [estão] diante de mim; \q há contenda, e a discórdia se levanta.
pt.B: Por que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} me fazes ver a maldade? Por que toleras a opressão? \q Destruição e violência estão diante de mim; \q surgem brigas e conflitos.
pt.R: Por que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} me fazes ver as pessoas praticando o mal? Por que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} apenas olhas enquanto elas causam sofrimento? \q Para onde quer que eu olhe, há destruição e violência. \q As pessoas discutem e brigam.

decisions.choice: iniquity and trouble: wickedness and the misery it causes
decisions.reason: The first word is wrongdoing, especially deceit and the abuse of power; the second is the trouble and suffering it brings on others. They are often paired (Psalm 10:7; Isaiah 10:1; Job 4:8).

decisions.choice: do you look on trouble?: God seems to watch and do nothing
alternatives: why do you make me look at trouble?
decisions.reason: The verb may mean "you look on" or "you make me look". The same verb is used of God in verse 13 ("why do you look on the treacherous?"), so it is taken here of God looking on without acting.

decisions.choice: strife and contention: quarrels and lawsuits
decisions.reason: The two words are used of quarrels and of disputes in court. They lead into verse 4, where the courts fail.

decisions.choice: put up with (B); just look on while (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what it means for God to "look on" trouble without stopping it (m2).

decisions.choice: "toleras" (B); "solo miras mientras" (R)
decisions.reason: Spanish B says what the looking implies, God seeming to put up with the wrong; R says he only watches.

source.text: עַל־כֵּן֙ תָּפ֣וּג תּוֹרָ֔ה וְלֹֽא־יֵצֵ֥א לָנֶ֖צַח מִשְׁפָּ֑ט כִּ֤י רָשָׁע֙ מַכְתִּ֣יר אֶת־הַצַּדִּ֔יק עַל־כֵּ֛ן יֵצֵ֥א מִשְׁפָּ֖ט מְעֻקָּֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore grows numb [the] instruction, and not goes forth to perpetuity justice; for [the] wicked surrounds the righteous; therefore justice goes forth perverted.

en.L: Therefore [the] instruction grows numb, \q and justice never goes forth; \q for [the] wicked surround the righteous; \q therefore justice goes forth twisted.
en.B: So the instruction loses its force, \q and justice never wins out. \q The wicked hem in the righteous, \q so justice comes out twisted.
en.R: That is why God's teaching has no power, \q and justice never wins. \q Wicked people surround those who do right, \q so justice is twisted.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi la loi s’engourdit, \q et le droit ne sort jamais ; \q car le méchant encercle le juste ; \q c’est pourquoi le droit sort tordu.
fr.B: Aussi l’instruction perd-elle sa force, \q et le droit ne triomphe jamais. \q Les méchants encerclent les justes, \q et le droit en sort faussé.
fr.R: Voilà pourquoi l’enseignement de Dieu n’a plus de force, \q et la justice ne gagne jamais. \q Les méchants entourent ceux qui font ce qui est juste, \q alors la justice est faussée.

es.L: Por tanto, la instrucción se debilita, \q y nunca sale el derecho; \q porque el impío rodea al justo, \q por tanto, sale torcido el derecho.
es.B: Por eso la instrucción pierde su fuerza, \q y el derecho nunca se impone. \q Los malvados acorralan a los justos, \q y por eso el derecho sale torcido.
es.R: Por eso la enseñanza de Dios no tiene poder, \q y la justicia nunca triunfa. \q La gente malvada rodea a los que hacen lo correcto, \q y así la justicia se tuerce.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo sheria inadhoofika, \q na hukumu haitoki kamwe; \q kwa maana mwovu anamzunguka mwenye haki; \q kwa hiyo hukumu inatoka ikiwa imepotoka.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo mafundisho yanapoteza nguvu, \q na haki haishindi kamwe. \q Waovu wanawazingira wenye haki, \q kwa hiyo haki inapotoshwa.
sw.R: Ndiyo sababu mafundisho ya Mungu hayana nguvu, \q na haki haishindi kamwe. \q Watu waovu wanawazunguka wale wanaotenda haki, \q kwa hiyo haki inapotoshwa.

vi.L: Vì thế lời dạy dỗ trở nên tê liệt, \q và công lý không bao giờ ra đến nơi; \q vì kẻ ác vây quanh người công chính; \q vì thế công lý ra đi bị bẻ cong.
vi.B: Vì vậy lời dạy dỗ mất hết sức mạnh, \q và công lý chẳng bao giờ thắng thế. \q Kẻ ác vây bọc người công chính, \q nên công lý bị bóp méo.
vi.R: Vì thế lời dạy của Đức Chúa Trời không còn hiệu lực, \q và công lý chẳng bao giờ thắng. \q Kẻ gian ác vây quanh người làm điều ngay thẳng, \q nên công lý bị bẻ cong.

ko.L: 그러므로 가르침이 힘을 잃고, \q 정의가 결코 나오지 않습니다. \q 악인이 의인을 에워싸기 때문입니다. \q 그러므로 정의가 굽어져 나옵니다.
ko.B: 그래서 가르침은 힘을 잃고, \q 정의는 끝내 이기지 못합니다. \q 악인들이 의인들을 둘러싸니, \q 정의가 굽어져 나옵니다.
ko.R: 그래서 하나님의 가르침이 아무 힘이 없습니다. \q 바른 판결은 끝내 내려지지 않습니다. \q 악한 사람들이 바르게 사는 사람들을 둘러싸고 있으니, \q 재판이 다 비뚤어집니다.

pt.L: Por isso a instrução se entorpece, \q e a justiça nunca sai; \q pois o ímpio cerca o justo; \q por isso a justiça sai torcida.
pt.B: Por isso a instrução perde a força, \q e a justiça nunca prevalece. \q Os ímpios cercam os justos, \q e assim a justiça sai distorcida.
pt.R: É por isso que o ensino de Deus não tem poder, \q e a justiça nunca vence. \q Os maus cercam os que fazem o que é certo, \q e por isso a justiça é torcida.

decisions.choice: instruction: God's teaching, as the rule of life and of the courts
decisions.reason: The word (*torah*) is God's instruction to his people: the teaching of the covenant, applied by priests and judges in settling disputes (Deuteronomy 17:8-11). When it "grows numb" it has lost its force: it no longer restrains anyone.

decisions.choice: grows numb ... justice never goes forth
decisions.reason: The verb means to grow numb or cold, to lose feeling and strength (Genesis 45:26; Psalm 77:3). The phrase "never goes forth" may also be read "never goes forth victorious": justice never comes out the winner.

decisions.choice: the wicked and the righteous: Habakkuk's complaint is about Judah
alternatives: the wicked are a foreign oppressor
decisions.reason: The wicked who surround the righteous are most likely the powerful in Judah who bend the courts against honest people, as in the complaints of Jeremiah (Jeremiah 5:26-28) and Amos (5:12). The LORD's answer, that he is sending the Chaldeans (verses 5-11), is his judgment on this injustice. Some take the wicked to be a foreign oppressor already here.

decisions.choice: instruction (L, B); God's teaching (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *torah* in the prophets: "instruction" at Literal and Balanced, "teaching" at Readable, which adds "God's" to say whose teaching it is.

decisions.choice: *torah* "la loi" (L), "l'instruction" (B), "l'enseignement de Dieu" (R); *mishpat* "le droit" (L, B), "la justice" (R)
decisions.reason: As the prophets in French: God's *torah* is "loi" / "instruction" / "enseignement", lowercase, since it is God's teaching in general, not the named Law of Moses; *mishpat* is "le droit" at L and B, as Isaiah, and plain "la justice" at R.

decisions.choice: "la instrucción" (L, B), "la enseñanza de Dios" (R); "el derecho" (L, B), "la justicia" (R)
decisions.reason: Torah is "instrucción" at L and B and "enseñanza" at R, as the Spanish Isaiah; mishpat is "derecho" at L and B, as the prophets' word pair, and plain "justicia" at R.

decisions.choice: "sheria" (L), "mafundisho" (B, R) for torah; "hukumu" (L), "haki" (B, R) for mishpat
decisions.reason: As the Psalms note and the Isaiah and Jeremiah blocks: torah here is God's instruction as the rule of life and of the courts, not only a law code.

decisions.choice: *torah* is "가르침" (L, B) and "하나님의 가르침" (R)
decisions.reason: As Isaiah and Jeremiah render *torah* in the prophets (Isa 1:10; 2:3): God's teaching, which also guided the courts; "율법" stays for the law of Moses as a code and for the Greek.

decisions.choice: "lời dạy dỗ" (L, B) / "lời dạy của Đức Chúa Trời" (R) for torah
decisions.reason: As Isaiah 1:10 in Vietnamese; "luật pháp" would narrow it to a code of law, while the meaning decision speaks of God's teaching as the rule of life and of the courts.

decisions.choice: a instrução (L, B); o ensino de Deus (R); a justiça
decisions.reason: As the English and as Jeremiah and Ezekiel have torah in Portuguese (m1): "instrução" at Literal and Balanced, "ensino" at Readable, with "de Deus" added as the English Readable adds "God's". Mishpat is "justiça" at every level, as in the prophets.

source.text: רְא֤וּ בַגּוֹיִם֙ וְֽהַבִּ֔יטוּ וְהִֽתַּמְּה֖וּ תְּמָ֑הוּ כִּי־פֹ֨עַל֙ פֹּעֵ֣ל בִּֽימֵיכֶ֔ם לֹ֥א תַאֲמִ֖ינוּ כִּ֥י יְסֻפָּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: See among [the] nations and look, and be astonished, be astounded; for a deed [I am] doing in your days; not you will believe if it is told.

en.L: Look among the nations, and watch, \q and be astonished, be astounded! \q For a work [I am] working in your days \q [that] you would not believe if it were told.
en.B: Look at the nations and watch, \q and be utterly astonished! \q For I am doing something in your days \q that you would not believe even if you were told.
en.R: Look at what is happening among the nations! \q Be amazed and astonished! \q I am about to do something in your lifetime \q that you would not believe even if someone told you.

fr.L: Regardez parmi les nations, et observez, \q et soyez étonnés, soyez stupéfaits ! \q Car [je] fais une œuvre en vos jours, \q vous ne [la] croiriez pas si elle était racontée.
fr.B: Regardez les nations et observez, \q soyez saisis de stupeur ! \q Car je fais en vos jours une œuvre \q que vous ne croiriez pas si on vous la racontait.
fr.R: Regardez ce qui se passe parmi les nations ! \q Soyez étonnés et stupéfaits ! \q Je vais faire de votre vivant quelque chose \q que vous ne croiriez pas, même si on vous le racontait.

es.L: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} entre las naciones, y {{plural_you:observen|observad}}, \q y {{plural_you:asómbrense|asombraos}}, {{plural_you:quédense atónitos|quedaos atónitos}}, \q porque una obra [estoy] haciendo en {{plural_you:sus días|vuestros días}} \q [que] no {{plural_you:creerían|creeríais}} si se contara.
es.B: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} entre las naciones y {{plural_you:observen|observad}}, \q ¡y {{plural_you:quédense|quedaos}} totalmente asombrados! \q Porque voy a hacer algo en {{plural_you:sus días|vuestros días}} \q que no {{plural_you:creerían|creeríais}} aunque alguien {{plural_you:se lo|os lo}} contara.
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} lo que pasa entre las naciones! \q ¡{{plural_you:Asómbrense|Asombraos}} y {{plural_you:quédense|quedaos}} con la boca abierta! \q Voy a hacer algo en {{plural_you:su tiempo|vuestro tiempo}} \q que no {{plural_you:creerían|creeríais}} aunque alguien {{plural_you:se lo|os lo}} contara.

sw.L: Tazameni katika mataifa, na angalieni, \q mkastaajabu, mstaajabu! \q Kwa maana kazi [ninaitenda] katika siku zenu \q [ambayo] hamngeiamini kama mngesimuliwa.
sw.B: Yatazameni mataifa na kuangalia, \q mshangae sana! \q Kwa maana ninafanya kazi katika siku zenu \q ambayo hamngeiamini hata kama mngeambiwa.
sw.R: Tazameni yanayotokea kati ya mataifa! \q Shangaeni na kustaajabu! \q Ninakaribia kufanya jambo wakati wa maisha yenu \q ambalo hamngeliamini hata mtu akiwaambia.

vi.L: Hãy nhìn giữa các nước và hãy xem, \q hãy kinh ngạc, hãy sửng sốt! \q Vì [{{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đang] làm một việc trong đời các ngươi \q [mà] các ngươi sẽ không tin nếu có ai kể lại.
vi.B: Hãy nhìn các nước và quan sát, \q rồi các ngươi sẽ vô cùng kinh ngạc! \q Vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đang làm một việc trong đời các ngươi, \q một việc mà dù có người kể lại, các ngươi cũng không tin.
vi.R: Hãy nhìn xem điều đang xảy ra giữa các nước! \q Hãy kinh ngạc và sửng sốt! \q Ta sắp làm một việc ngay trong đời các ngươi, \q một việc mà dù có ai kể cho các ngươi nghe, các ngươi cũng không tin.

ko.L: 민족들 가운데서 보고 바라보아라. \q 놀라고 또 놀라라! \q 너희의 날에 내가 한 일을 [하고 있으니], \q 그것을 누가 말해 주어도 너희가 믿지 못할 것이다.
ko.B: 민족들을 눈여겨보아라. \q 보고 몹시 놀라라! \q 너희가 사는 날에 내가 한 가지 일을 하고 있다. \q 누가 그 일을 말해 주어도 너희는 믿지 못할 것이다.
ko.R: 민족들 가운데서 일어나는 일을 보아라! \q 보고 깜짝 놀라라! \q 너희가 살아 있는 동안에 내가 어떤 일을 하려고 한다. \q 누가 그 일을 말해 주어도 너희는 믿지 않을 것이다.

pt.L: Vejam entre as nações e observem, \q e maravilhem-se, fiquem pasmados! \q Pois [eu] realizo uma obra nos dias de vocês, \q [em que] vocês não crerão, se for contada.
pt.B: Olhem para as nações e observem, \q e fiquem espantados, muito espantados! \q Pois estou realizando uma obra nos dias de vocês, \q em que vocês não creriam, mesmo que alguém a contasse a vocês.
pt.R: Olhem o que está acontecendo entre as nações! \q Fiquem espantados e admirados! \q Eu vou fazer uma coisa no tempo de vocês \q em que vocês não acreditariam, mesmo que alguém contasse isso a vocês.

decisions.choice: the LORD answers: "I am doing a work"
decisions.reason: The speaker changes: the LORD answers Habakkuk's complaint. "You" is plural, Habakkuk and his people. The Hebrew says "doing a work" without naming who does it; verse 6 shows that it is the LORD ("I am raising up").

decisions.choice: be astonished, be astounded: the same verb twice, for emphasis
decisions.reason: The verb is repeated in two forms, a Hebrew way of saying "be utterly amazed". The shock is that God will answer the injustice in Judah by bringing the Babylonians.

decisions.choice: Acts 13:41 quotes this verse in its Greek form
decisions.reason: At the end of his sermon in Pisidian Antioch, Paul warns his hearers with this verse: "Look, you scoffers, and wonder, and perish, for I am working a work in your days" (Acts 13:41). He quotes the Greek translation, which has "you scoffers" where the Hebrew has "among the nations" (the Hebrew words are close in form) and adds "perish". As in Habakkuk, the warning is that God is doing something that his hearers would not believe.

decisions.choice: [I am] (L); I am (B)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew leaves out the subject of "working"; Literal brackets "I am", and Balanced and Readable write it, following verse 6 (m1).

decisions.choice: "une œuvre en vos jours" (L, B)
decisions.reason: Acts 13:41 quotes this verse; French keeps the published Acts' key words "une œuvre en vos jours" where the Hebrew means the same, without Acts' Greek-only wording ("vous qui méprisez").

decisions.choice: plural_you spans on every verb and possessive
decisions.reason: God answers the people as a group, so the plural "you" takes the plural_you setting; "Miren entre las naciones" is kept as the term sheet asks, so that Acts 13:41 ("Miren") can be seen.

decisions.choice: "[estoy]", "[que]"
decisions.reason: Words Spanish needs that the Hebrew leaves unsaid are bracketed at L.

decisions.choice: "kazi ... katika siku zenu ... hamngeiamini" (L, B)
decisions.reason: Acts 13:41 quotes this verse from the Greek; the shared words "kazi", "katika siku zenu" and "hamngeiamini" are kept as the Swahili Acts words them, while "Tazameni katika mataifa" follows the Hebrew, where Acts has "you scoffers".

decisions.choice: The LORD answers in 해라체 ("보아라", "놀라라"); the doubled verb is "놀라고 또 놀라라" (L), "몹시 놀라라" (B), "깜짝 놀라라" (R)
decisions.reason: Korean cannot repeat one verb stem as the Hebrew does without sounding broken, so Literal joins the two with "또" and the other levels give the emphasis with an adverb. Acts 13:41 quotes the Greek form ("멸시하는 자들아"); the Hebrew "among the nations" is kept here.

decisions.choice: the LORD answers the people with "các ngươi" and calls himself "Ta"
decisions.reason: The verbs are plural: God addresses the people of Judah, not Habakkuk alone, so the oracle's "các ngươi" is used. The allusion decision's Acts 13:41 has the same "trong đời các ngươi ... không tin".

decisions.choice: Vejam (L) / Olhem (B, R); maravilhem-se (L) / fiquem espantados (B, R); realizo uma obra nos dias de vocês (L) / estou realizando uma obra nos dias de vocês (B) / no tempo de vocês (R); crer (L, B) / acreditar (R)
decisions.reason: Paul quotes this verse in Acts 13:41 from the Greek translation (m3), which has "desprezadores" and "desapareçam" where the Hebrew has "entre as nações" and a second verb of astonishment. Each level follows the Hebrew and keeps the Portuguese of Acts 13:41 for the words the two share: "Vejam ... maravilhem-se" (L), "Olhem ... fiquem espantados" (B), "realizo uma obra nos dias de vocês", "crer" (L, B) and "acreditar ... mesmo que alguém contasse isso a vocês" (R). God speaks to the prophet and his people together, so "vocês" (m1).

source.text: כִּֽי־הִנְנִ֤י מֵקִים֙ אֶת־הַכַּשְׂדִּ֔ים הַגּ֖וֹי הַמַּ֣ר וְהַנִּמְהָ֑ר הַֽהוֹלֵךְ֙ לְמֶרְחֲבֵי־אֶ֔רֶץ לָרֶ֖שֶׁת מִשְׁכָּנ֥וֹת לֹּא־לֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: For look, I [am] raising up the Chaldeans, the nation the bitter and the impetuous, the [one] going to [the] breadths of [the] earth to possess dwellings not to it.

en.L: For look, I am raising up the Chaldeans, \q that bitter and impetuous nation, \q who march through the breadth of the earth \q to take possession of dwellings [that are] not theirs.
en.B: For I am raising up the Chaldeans, \q that fierce and reckless nation, \q who sweep across the wide earth \q to seize homes that are not their own.
en.R: I am bringing the Babylonians to power. \q They are cruel and quick to attack. \q They march across the whole earth \q to take over homes that belong to other people.

fr.L: Car voici, je fais lever les Chaldéens, \q cette nation amère et impétueuse, \q qui marche à travers les étendues de la terre \q pour s’emparer de demeures [qui ne sont] pas à elle.
fr.B: Car je suscite les Chaldéens, \q cette nation féroce et fougueuse, \q qui parcourt la terre dans toute son étendue \q pour s’emparer de demeures qui ne lui appartiennent pas.
fr.R: Je vais donner le pouvoir aux Babyloniens. \q Ils sont cruels et prompts à attaquer. \q Ils traversent toute la terre \q pour prendre les maisons des autres.

es.L: Porque he aquí, yo levanto a los caldeos, \q esa nación cruel e impetuosa, \q que marcha por la anchura de la tierra \q para tomar posesión de moradas [que] no [son] suyas.
es.B: Porque yo levanto a los caldeos, \q esa nación feroz y temeraria, \q que avanza por toda la extensión de la tierra \q para apoderarse de hogares ajenos.
es.R: Voy a darles poder a los babilonios. \q Son crueles y rápidos para atacar. \q Marchan por toda la tierra \q para quedarse con las casas de otros.

sw.L: Kwa maana tazama, ninawainua Wakaldayo, \q taifa lile kali na lenye haraka, \q linalopita katika upana wa dunia \q kumiliki makao yasiyo [yake].
sw.B: Kwa maana ninawainua Wakaldayo, \q taifa lile katili na lenye pupa, \q linalopita katika dunia yote pana \q kunyakua makao yasiyo yake.
sw.R: Ninawapa Wababeli nguvu. \q Wao ni wakatili na wepesi kushambulia. \q Wanapita katika dunia yote \q kunyakua nyumba za watu wengine.

vi.L: Vì kìa, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đang dấy lên người Canh-đê, \q dân tộc hung bạo và hấp tấp ấy, \q là dân đi khắp bề rộng của đất \q để chiếm lấy những chỗ ở không phải của mình.
vi.B: Vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đang dấy lên người Canh-đê, \q dân tộc tàn bạo và liều lĩnh ấy, \q chúng tràn qua khắp mặt đất rộng lớn \q để cướp lấy nhà cửa không thuộc về mình.
vi.R: Ta đang làm cho người Ba-by-lôn trở nên hùng mạnh. \q Chúng tàn ác và tấn công rất nhanh. \q Chúng kéo quân đi khắp mặt đất \q để chiếm lấy nhà cửa của các dân khác.

ko.L: 보라, 내가 갈대아 사람들을 일으키고 있다. \q 그 사납고 성급한 민족, \q 땅의 넓은 곳들로 행진하여 \q 자기 것이 아닌 거처들을 차지하는 [민족이다].
ko.B: 내가 갈대아 사람들을 일으키겠다. \q 그들은 사납고 거침없는 민족이다. \q 넓은 땅을 휩쓸고 다니며 \q 남의 집들을 빼앗는다.
ko.R: 내가 바빌로니아 사람들을 강하게 하겠다. \q 그들은 잔인하고 재빨리 쳐들어온다. \q 그들은 온 땅을 누비며 \q 다른 사람들의 집을 빼앗는다.

pt.L: Pois eis que eu levanto os caldeus, \q aquela nação amarga e impetuosa, \q que marcha pelas extensões da terra \q para tomar posse de moradas que não [são] suas.
pt.B: Pois estou levantando os caldeus, \q essa nação feroz e impetuosa, \q que avança pela vastidão da terra \q para se apoderar de moradas que não lhe pertencem.
pt.R: Vou dar poder aos babilônios. \q Eles são cruéis e rápidos para atacar. \q Marcham pela terra inteira \q para tomar casas que pertencem a outros.

decisions.choice: the Chaldeans: the Babylonians
decisions.reason: The Chaldeans were a people of southern Babylonia. A Chaldean dynasty took power in Babylon in 626 BC under Nabopolassar, helped to destroy Nineveh in 612 BC, and under Nebuchadnezzar defeated Egypt at Carchemish in 605 BC. Babylon then ruled Judah, took Jerusalem in 597 BC and destroyed it in 587/586 BC.

decisions.choice: I am raising up: God uses a pagan nation as his instrument
decisions.reason: The LORD says that it is he who raises up the Babylonians, as he called Assyria "the rod of my anger" (Isaiah 10:5) and Nebuchadnezzar "my servant" (Jeremiah 25:9). This answer troubles Habakkuk even more, and leads to his second complaint (1:12-17): how can a holy God use a nation more wicked than those it punishes?

decisions.choice: bitter and impetuous: savage and swift
decisions.reason: "Bitter" means fierce and cruel, like a bear robbed of its cubs (2 Samuel 17:8; Judges 18:25). "Impetuous" is hasty, rushing ahead without restraint.

decisions.choice: the Babylonians (R)
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah and Jeremiah, Literal and Balanced say "Chaldeans" and Readable says "Babylonians". Readable says "bringing ... to power" for "raising up".

decisions.choice: "les Chaldéens" (L, B); "les Babyloniens" (R)
decisions.reason: As the French prophets and 2 Kings 25: the people's own name at Literal and Balanced, the name a new reader knows at Readable, as the English.

decisions.choice: "los caldeos" (L, B); "los babilonios" (R)
decisions.reason: As in the Spanish Isaiah and Jeremiah, the people's name is kept at L and B and explained at R.

decisions.choice: "cruel" for "bitter"
decisions.reason: Hebrew "bitter" here means savage; Spanish "amarga" would not say that of a nation, so L already uses "cruel".

decisions.choice: "Wakaldayo" (L, B); "Wababeli" (R)
decisions.reason: As 2 Chronicles 36:17 and the Jeremiah block: the Chaldeans keep their name at L and B, and Readable names them as the Babylonians, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: The Chaldeans are "갈대아 사람들" (L, B) and "바빌로니아 사람들" (R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording, as 2 Kings 25 and Jeremiah; Readable names the people the English Readable names.

decisions.choice: os caldeus (L, B); os babilônios (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: as Jeremiah 21:4 and Isaiah set the name in Portuguese (m1), "os caldeus" at Literal and Balanced and "os babilônios" at Readable, as the English does.

source.text: אָיֹ֥ם וְנוֹרָ֖א ה֑וּא מִמֶּ֕נּוּ מִשְׁפָּט֥וֹ וּשְׂאֵת֖וֹ יֵצֵֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: Terrifying and fearsome [is] it; from itself its justice and its dignity go forth.

en.L: Dreadful and fearsome [is] it; \q from itself its justice and its dignity go forth.
en.B: They are feared and dreaded; \q they set their own law and claim their own honor.
en.R: People are terrified of them. \q They make their own rules and answer to no one.

fr.L: Terrible et redoutable [est]-elle ; \q d’elle-même sortent son droit et sa dignité.
fr.B: Ils sont craints et redoutés ; \q ils fixent eux-mêmes leur loi et réclament leur propre honneur.
fr.R: Tout le monde a terriblement peur d’eux. \q Ils font leurs propres règles et ne rendent de comptes à personne.

es.L: Terrible y temible [es] ella; \q de sí misma salen su derecho y su dignidad.
es.B: Son temidos y espantosos; \q ellos mismos se dictan su ley y reclaman su propia honra.
es.R: La gente les tiene terror. \q Hacen sus propias reglas y no dan cuentas a nadie.

sw.L: [Ni] la kutisha na la kuogofya; \q kutoka kwake lenyewe hukumu yake na heshima yake vinatoka.
sw.B: Wanaogopwa na kuhofiwa; \q wanajiwekea sheria yao wenyewe na kujidai heshima yao wenyewe.
sw.R: Watu wanawaogopa sana. \q Wanajitungia sheria zao wenyewe, wala hawamtii mtu yeyote.

vi.L: Nó đáng khiếp và đáng sợ; \q công lý của nó và uy thế của nó ra từ chính nó.
vi.B: Chúng thật đáng khiếp sợ; \q chúng tự đặt ra luật mình và tự đòi lấy vinh dự cho mình.
vi.R: Người ta rất kinh hãi chúng. \q Chúng tự đặt ra luật lệ và chẳng phải chịu trách nhiệm với ai.

ko.L: 그것은 무섭고 두려우며, \q 그것에게서 그것의 정의와 그것의 위엄이 나온다.
ko.B: 그들은 무섭고 두려운 자들이다. \q 그들은 자기들 마음대로 법을 정하고 스스로 위엄을 내세운다.
ko.R: 사람들은 그들을 몹시 무서워한다. \q 그들은 자기들 마음대로 규칙을 만들고 누구의 말도 듣지 않는다.

pt.L: Terrível e temível [é] ela; \q dela mesma procedem a sua justiça e a sua dignidade.
pt.B: Eles são temidos e terríveis; \q fazem a sua própria lei e reclamam a sua própria honra.
pt.R: As pessoas têm pavor deles. \q Eles fazem as suas próprias regras e não prestam contas a ninguém.

decisions.choice: from itself its justice and its dignity go forth: it answers to no one
decisions.reason: The nation decides for itself what is right and claims its own greatness; it recognizes no law above its own will. The word "justice" picks up verse 4: Judah's justice is twisted, and the justice of the Babylonians is whatever they decide.

decisions.choice: they (B, R) for "it"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of the nation as "it" (or "he"). Balanced and Readable say "they", the Babylonians, which reads more naturally in English and does not change the sense.

decisions.choice: "elle" (L), agreeing with "nation"; "ils" (B, R), the Chaldeans
alternatives: "il" at L, as the Hebrew masculine
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of the nation as "it"; French "nation" is feminine, so Literal says "elle" through verse 11, and Balanced and Readable say "ils", as the English "they".

decisions.choice: "ella" for the nation
decisions.reason: At L the pronoun agrees with "nación" (feminine in Spanish), keeping the Hebrew singular; B and R say "they", as the English does.

decisions.choice: "nó" (L) / "chúng" (B, R) for the nation
decisions.reason: The terms note: a nation is "nó", kept at Literal; Balanced and Readable speak of the people with "chúng", the pronoun for enemies in the oracles.

decisions.choice: ela (L); eles (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the singular of the Hebrew, and Portuguese "nação" makes it "ela", which reads naturally; Balanced and Readable say "eles", the Chaldeans, as the English says "they".

source.text: וְקַלּ֨וּ מִנְּמֵרִ֜ים סוּסָ֗יו וְחַדּוּ֙ מִזְּאֵ֣בֵי עֶ֔רֶב וּפָ֖שׁוּ פָּֽרָשָׁ֑יו וּפָֽרָשָׁיו֙ מֵרָח֣וֹק יָבֹ֔אוּ יָעֻ֕פוּ כְּנֶ֖שֶׁר חָ֥שׁ לֶאֱכֽוֹל׃

records.literal_gloss: And swifter than leopards [are] its horses, and fiercer than wolves of [the] evening; and its horsemen gallop, and its horsemen from afar come; they fly like an eagle hastening to devour.

en.L: Swifter than leopards [are] its horses, and fiercer than wolves of [the] evening; \q and its horsemen gallop proudly; \q and its horsemen come from afar; \q they fly like an eagle hurrying to devour.
en.B: Their horses are swifter than leopards, \q fiercer than wolves at dusk. \q Their horsemen charge ahead; \q their riders come from far away; \q they swoop like an eagle rushing to devour.
en.R: Their horses are faster than leopards \q and fiercer than hungry wolves at sunset. \q Their soldiers on horseback charge ahead. \q They come from far away. \q They swoop down like eagles rushing to catch their food.

fr.L: Plus rapides que des léopards [sont] ses chevaux, et plus féroces que des loups du soir ; \q et ses cavaliers galopent fièrement ; \q et ses cavaliers viennent de loin ; \q ils volent comme un aigle qui se hâte de dévorer.
fr.B: Leurs chevaux sont plus rapides que des léopards, \q plus féroces que des loups au crépuscule. \q Leurs cavaliers chargent ; \q leurs cavaliers viennent de loin ; \q ils fondent comme l’aigle qui se précipite pour dévorer.
fr.R: Leurs chevaux sont plus rapides que des léopards \q et plus féroces que des loups affamés à la tombée de la nuit. \q Leurs soldats à cheval foncent en avant. \q Ils viennent de loin. \q Ils fondent sur leur proie comme des aigles qui se précipitent pour attraper leur nourriture.

es.L: Más veloces que leopardos [son] sus caballos, y más feroces que lobos de [la] tarde; \q y sus jinetes galopan con arrogancia; \q y sus jinetes vienen de lejos; \q vuelan como águila que se apresura a devorar.
es.B: Sus caballos son más veloces que los leopardos, \q más feroces que los lobos al anochecer. \q Sus jinetes se lanzan al ataque; \q sus jinetes vienen de lejos; \q se abalanzan como el águila que se apresura a devorar.
es.R: Sus caballos son más rápidos que los leopardos \q y más feroces que los lobos hambrientos al atardecer. \q Sus soldados a caballo se lanzan al ataque. \q Vienen desde muy lejos. \q Se lanzan como águilas que bajan a toda prisa a atrapar su comida.

sw.L: Farasi wake [ni] wepesi kuliko chui, na wakali kuliko mbwa mwitu wa jioni; \q na wapanda farasi wake wanakimbia kwa kiburi; \q na wapanda farasi wake wanakuja kutoka mbali; \q wanaruka kama tai anayeharakisha kula.
sw.B: Farasi wao ni wepesi kuliko chui, \q wakali kuliko mbwa mwitu wakati wa jioni. \q Wapanda farasi wao wanashambulia mbele; \q askari wao wa farasi wanakuja kutoka mbali; \q wanashuka kwa kasi kama tai anayewahi kula mawindo.
sw.R: Farasi wao wana mbio kuliko chui, \q na ni wakali kuliko mbwa mwitu wenye njaa wakati wa machweo. \q Askari wao wapanda farasi wanashambulia mbele. \q Wanakuja kutoka mbali. \q Wanashuka kwa kasi kama tai wanaowahi kukamata chakula chao.

vi.L: Ngựa của nó nhanh hơn beo, và dữ hơn sói lúc chiều tối; \q kỵ binh của nó phi nước đại kiêu hãnh; \q kỵ binh của nó đến từ xa; \q chúng bay như chim đại bàng vội vã lao xuống để ăn mồi.
vi.B: Ngựa của chúng nhanh hơn beo, \q hung dữ hơn sói lúc chạng vạng. \q Kỵ binh chúng xông lên phía trước; \q quân cưỡi ngựa của chúng đến từ phương xa; \q chúng sà xuống như đại bàng lao vào xé mồi.
vi.R: Ngựa của chúng chạy nhanh hơn beo, \q và hung dữ hơn bầy sói đói lúc mặt trời lặn. \q Lính cưỡi ngựa của chúng xông lên. \q Chúng đến từ rất xa. \q Chúng lao xuống như chim đại bàng vồ lấy mồi.

ko.L: 그것의 말들은 표범보다 빠르고, 저녁 이리들보다 사나우며, \q 그것의 기병들은 뽐내며 달린다. \q 그것의 기병들이 먼 곳에서 오며, \q 먹이를 삼키려고 서두르는 독수리처럼 날아온다.
ko.B: 그들의 말은 표범보다 빠르고, \q 해 질 녘의 이리보다 사납다. \q 그들의 기병은 앞으로 내달린다. \q 그들의 기병이 먼 곳에서 온다. \q 그들은 먹이를 삼키려고 덮치는 독수리처럼 날아든다.
ko.R: 그들의 말은 표범보다 빠르고 \q 해 질 녘에 굶주린 이리보다 사납다. \q 말 탄 군인들이 앞으로 달려 나간다. \q 그들은 먼 곳에서 온다. \q 그들은 먹이를 잡으려고 내리꽂히는 독수리처럼 덮쳐 온다.

pt.L: Mais ligeiros que leopardos [são] os seus cavalos, e mais ferozes que lobos da tarde; \q e os seus cavaleiros galopam com arrogância; \q e os seus cavaleiros vêm de longe; \q voam como águia que se apressa a devorar.
pt.B: Os seus cavalos são mais velozes que leopardos, \q mais ferozes que lobos ao anoitecer. \q Os seus cavaleiros avançam em disparada; \q os seus soldados a cavalo vêm de longe; \q mergulham como uma águia que se lança para devorar.
pt.R: Os seus cavalos são mais rápidos que leopardos \q e mais ferozes que lobos famintos ao pôr do sol. \q Os seus soldados a cavalo avançam em disparada. \q Eles vêm de longe. \q Descem como águias que se lançam para pegar a sua comida.

decisions.choice: wolves of the evening: hungry wolves hunting at dusk
decisions.reason: Wolves hunt at nightfall after a day without food (Zephaniah 3:3; Jeremiah 5:6). The leopard, the wolf and the eagle are the swiftest and fiercest hunters the hearers knew.

decisions.choice: its horsemen gallop proudly
decisions.reason: The verb is rare and its sense is uncertain: it may mean to gallop, to paw the ground, or to spread out. The word for horsemen is repeated in the next line; the first may mean "horses" or "chargers".

decisions.choice: an eagle: a great bird of prey
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word covers the eagle and the vulture. It is the bird that swoops on its prey from a great height (Deuteronomy 28:49; Jeremiah 48:40).

decisions.choice: Their horses (B, R); charge ahead (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "their" for "its" (see verse 7). "Charge ahead" gives the sense of the uncertain verb (m2). Readable adds "hungry" (m1) and "to catch their food".

source.text: כֻּלֹּה֙ לְחָמָ֣ס יָב֔וֹא מְגַמַּ֥ת פְּנֵיהֶ֖ם קָדִ֑ימָה וַיֶּאֱסֹ֥ף כַּח֖וֹל שֶֽׁבִי׃

records.literal_gloss: All of it for violence comes; the totality of their faces [is] forward; and it gathers like sand captives.

en.L: All of it comes for violence; \q the mass of their faces [is set] forward; \q and it gathers captives like sand.
en.B: They all come intent on violence; \q their faces are set straight ahead, \q and they gather captives like sand.
en.R: They all come to do violence. \q Their army keeps pressing forward, \q and they take more prisoners than anyone can count.

fr.L: Tout entière elle vient pour la violence ; \q l’ensemble de leurs visages [est tourné] en avant ; \q et elle amasse des captifs comme du sable.
fr.B: Ils viennent tous, avides de violence ; \q leurs visages sont tournés droit devant, \q et ils ramassent des captifs comme du sable.
fr.R: Ils viennent tous pour commettre des violences. \q Leur armée avance sans cesse, \q et ils font plus de prisonniers qu’on ne peut en compter.

es.L: Todo él viene para la violencia; \q la multitud de sus rostros [está puesta] hacia adelante; \q y recoge cautivos como arena.
es.B: Todos vienen decididos a la violencia; \q sus rostros miran fijamente hacia adelante, \q y reúnen cautivos como arena.
es.R: Todos vienen a hacer violencia. \q Su ejército sigue avanzando, \q y toman más prisioneros de los que se pueden contar.

sw.L: Lote linakuja kwa ajili ya dhuluma; \q wingi wa nyuso zao [umeelekezwa] mbele; \q nalo linakusanya mateka kama mchanga.
sw.B: Wote wanakuja wakiwa wamenuia dhuluma; \q nyuso zao zimeelekezwa mbele moja kwa moja, \q nao wanakusanya mateka kama mchanga.
sw.R: Wote wanakuja kufanya dhuluma. \q Jeshi lao linazidi kusonga mbele, \q nao wanachukua mateka wengi kuliko mtu yeyote anavyoweza kuhesabu.

vi.L: Tất cả nó đến vì bạo lực; \q toàn thể mặt chúng [hướng] về phía trước; \q và nó gom tù binh như cát.
vi.B: Tất cả chúng đều kéo đến để làm điều tàn bạo; \q mặt chúng nhắm thẳng về phía trước, \q và chúng gom tù binh đông như cát.
vi.R: Tất cả chúng đều đến để làm điều tàn bạo. \q Đạo quân của chúng cứ tiến tới, \q và chúng bắt tù binh nhiều không đếm được.

ko.L: 그것은 모두 폭력을 위해 온다. \q 그들의 얼굴들의 무리가 앞쪽으로 [향해 있다]. \q 그것은 모래처럼 포로를 모은다.
ko.B: 그들은 모두 폭력을 휘두르러 온다. \q 그들은 얼굴을 앞으로만 향하고, \q 포로들을 모래처럼 많이 모은다.
ko.R: 그들은 모두 폭력을 휘두르려고 온다. \q 그들의 군대는 쉬지 않고 앞으로 밀고 나아간다. \q 그들은 셀 수 없이 많은 사람들을 포로로 잡아간다.

pt.L: Toda ela vem para a violência; \q a massa dos seus rostos [está voltada] para a frente; \q e ajunta cativos como areia.
pt.B: Todos eles vêm decididos a praticar violência; \q os seus rostos estão voltados para a frente, \q e eles ajuntam cativos como areia.
pt.R: Todos eles vêm para praticar violência. \q O seu exército continua avançando, \q e eles fazem mais prisioneiros do que se pode contar.

decisions.choice: the mass of their faces [is set] forward: a very uncertain line
alternatives: their faces are like the east wind
decisions.reason: The first word is used only here and its meaning is not known; it may mean "the whole", "the throng" or "the eagerness". The last word means "eastward" or "forward"; with a small change it is "the east wind", the scorching wind from the desert (Jeremiah 18:17). The line may say that the whole army faces forward, or that their faces are like the east wind. Either way the army advances without turning aside.

decisions.choice: captives like sand: countless captives
decisions.reason: Sand is the common picture of a number too great to count (Genesis 22:17; Judges 7:12).

decisions.choice: They all (B, R); their faces are set straight ahead (B); keeps pressing forward (R); more prisoners than anyone can count (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow the reading in m1 and say "they" for "it". Readable explains "like sand".

source.text: וְהוּא֙ בַּמְּלָכִ֣ים יִתְקַלָּ֔ס וְרֹזְנִ֖ים מִשְׂחָ֣ק ל֑וֹ ה֚וּא לְכָל־מִבְצָ֣ר יִשְׂחָ֔ק וַיִּצְבֹּ֥ר עָפָ֖ר וַֽיִּלְכְּדָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it at kings scoffs, and rulers [are] a laughingstock to it; it at every fortress laughs, and it heaps up earth and captures it.

en.L: And it scoffs at kings, \q and rulers [are] a joke to it; \q it laughs at every fortress, \q and heaps up earth and captures it.
en.B: They scoff at kings \q and make fun of rulers; \q they laugh at every fortress, \q for they pile up earth and take it.
en.R: They make fun of kings \q and laugh at rulers. \q They laugh at every fort, \q because they build ramps of earth and capture it.

fr.L: Et elle se moque des rois, \q et les dignitaires [sont] un jeu pour elle ; \q elle rit de toute forteresse, \q et elle entasse de la terre et la prend.
fr.B: Ils se moquent des rois \q et tournent les princes en dérision ; \q ils rient de toute forteresse, \q car ils entassent de la terre et la prennent.
fr.R: Ils se moquent des rois \q et rient des dirigeants. \q Ils rient de toutes les forteresses, \q parce qu’ils construisent des rampes de terre et s’en emparent.

es.L: Y él se burla de los reyes, \q y los gobernantes [son] para él cosa de risa; \q se ríe de toda fortaleza, \q y amontona tierra y la toma.
es.B: Se burlan de los reyes \q y se ríen de los gobernantes; \q se ríen de toda fortaleza, \q porque amontonan tierra y la toman.
es.R: Se burlan de los reyes \q y se ríen de los gobernantes. \q Se ríen de todas las fortalezas, \q porque construyen rampas de tierra y las conquistan.

sw.L: Nalo linawadhihaki wafalme, \q na watawala [ni] mzaha kwake; \q linaicheka kila ngome, \q nalo linarundika udongo na kuiteka.
sw.B: Wanawadhihaki wafalme \q na kuwafanyia watawala mzaha; \q wanaicheka kila ngome, \q kwa maana wanarundika udongo na kuiteka.
sw.R: Wanawadhihaki wafalme \q na kuwacheka watawala. \q Wanaicheka kila ngome, \q kwa sababu wanajenga vilima vya udongo na kuiteka.

vi.L: Nó nhạo báng các vua, \q và các người cầm quyền [là] trò cười cho nó; \q nó cười mọi đồn lũy, \q và đắp đất lên rồi chiếm lấy.
vi.B: Chúng chế giễu các vua \q và chế nhạo những người cầm quyền; \q chúng cười cợt mọi thành lũy, \q vì chúng đắp đất lên mà chiếm lấy.
vi.R: Chúng chế giễu các vua \q và cười nhạo những người cai trị. \q Chúng cười chê mọi đồn lũy, \q vì chúng đắp những con dốc bằng đất rồi chiếm lấy.

ko.L: 그것이 왕들을 비웃고, \q 통치자들은 그것에게 웃음거리[이다]. \q 그것은 모든 요새를 비웃고, \q 흙을 쌓아 올려 그것을 점령한다.
ko.B: 그들은 왕들을 비웃고 \q 통치자들을 놀림감으로 삼는다. \q 그들은 모든 요새를 우습게 여긴다. \q 흙을 쌓아 올려 그것을 빼앗기 때문이다.
ko.R: 그들은 왕들을 놀리고 \q 통치자들을 비웃는다. \q 그들은 어떤 요새를 보아도 웃는다. \q 흙을 쌓아 언덕을 만들고 그 요새를 빼앗기 때문이다.

pt.L: E ela zomba dos reis, \q e governantes [são] motivo de riso para ela; \q ela ri de toda fortaleza, \q e amontoa terra e a toma.
pt.B: Eles zombam dos reis \q e fazem pouco dos governantes; \q riem de toda fortaleza, \q pois amontoam terra e a tomam.
pt.R: Eles caçoam dos reis \q e riem dos governantes. \q Riem de todos os fortes, \q porque fazem rampas de terra e os conquistam.

decisions.choice: heaps up earth: builds a siege ramp
decisions.reason: Attackers piled earth and rubble against a city wall to make a ramp up which soldiers and battering rams could advance (2 Samuel 20:15; 2 Kings 19:32; Jeremiah 32:24). No fortress could keep the Babylonians out.

decisions.choice: build ramps of earth
decisions.reason: Readable says what heaping up earth is for (m1).

source.text: אָ֣ז חָלַ֥ף ר֛וּחַ וַֽיַּעֲבֹ֖ר וְאָשֵׁ֑ם ז֥וּ כֹח֖וֹ לֵאלֹהֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Then sweeps on [the] wind and passes on, and he becomes guilty, this [one whose] strength [is] his god.

en.L: Then [it] sweeps on [like the] wind and passes through, and it becomes guilty, \q this one whose strength [is] its god.
en.B: Then they sweep past like the wind and go on, guilty men \q whose own strength is their god.
en.R: Then they rush on like the wind and keep going. \q They are guilty, because they worship their own strength.

fr.L: Alors [elle] passe [comme le] vent et traverse, et elle se rend coupable, \q elle dont la force [est] son dieu.
fr.B: Puis ils passent comme le vent et poursuivent leur route, des hommes coupables \q dont la force est leur dieu.
fr.R: Puis ils filent comme le vent et continuent leur chemin. \q Ils sont coupables, car ils adorent leur propre force.

es.L: Entonces pasa [como el] viento y sigue adelante, y se hace culpable, \q este cuya fuerza [es] su dios.
es.B: Luego pasan como el viento y siguen de largo, hombres culpables \q cuyo dios es su propia fuerza.
es.R: Después pasan como el viento y siguen su camino. \q Son culpables, porque adoran su propia fuerza.

sw.L: Kisha [linapita] kwa kasi [kama] upepo na kupita, nalo linakuwa na hatia, \q huyu ambaye nguvu yake [ni] mungu wake.
sw.B: Kisha wanapita kwa kasi kama upepo na kuendelea, watu wenye hatia \q ambao nguvu yao wenyewe ndiyo mungu wao.
sw.R: Kisha wanapita kwa kasi kama upepo na kuendelea mbele. \q Wana hatia, kwa sababu wanaiabudu nguvu yao wenyewe.

vi.L: Rồi [nó] lướt qua [như] gió và đi qua, và nó mắc tội, \q kẻ này [là kẻ] lấy sức mình làm thần của mình.
vi.B: Rồi chúng lướt qua như gió và đi tiếp, những kẻ mắc tội \q tôn sức mạnh của mình làm thần.
vi.R: Rồi chúng ào qua như gió và cứ tiến tới. \q Chúng mắc tội, vì chúng thờ lạy chính sức mạnh của mình.

ko.L: 그때에 [그것이] 바람[처럼] 휩쓸고 지나가며 죄를 짓는다. \q 자기 힘이 자기 신인 이 [자가].
ko.B: 그러고는 바람처럼 휩쓸고 지나간다. 자기 힘을 신으로 삼는 \q 이 죄 있는 자들이다.
ko.R: 그러고 나서 그들은 바람처럼 휩쓸고 지나간다. \q 그들은 죄가 있다. 자기들의 힘을 신처럼 섬기기 때문이다.

pt.L: Então passa [como o] vento e atravessa, e se torna culpada, \q esta cuja força [é] o seu deus.
pt.B: Então passam como o vento e seguem adiante, homens culpados \q cuja própria força é o seu deus.
pt.R: Então eles passam correndo como o vento e continuam o seu caminho. \q Eles são culpados, porque adoram a sua própria força.

decisions.choice: then it sweeps on like the wind
alternatives: then the wind sweeps on and passes by
decisions.reason: The Hebrew can be read "then the wind sweeps on and passes" or "then it sweeps on like the wind". The second reading, taken here, compares the army to a wind that sweeps through and is gone (Isaiah 21:1).

decisions.choice: and it becomes guilty
alternatives: and he makes his own strength his god (Qumran commentary)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "and he becomes guilty". The commentary on Habakkuk found among the Dead Sea Scrolls reads a different verb, "and he sets" (his strength as his god), and some follow it. The translation keeps the Hebrew text.

decisions.choice: whose strength is his god: self-worship
decisions.reason: The Babylonians trust in and worship their own might. This is the charge on which their judgment will rest: the LORD has used them, but they owe their success to no god but their own power (Isaiah 10:13-15; Habakkuk 1:16; 2:4-5).

decisions.choice: guilty men whose own strength is their god (B); they worship their own strength (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "they" for the singular "it" or "he". Readable makes plain that treating one's strength as god means worshiping it.

source.text: הֲל֧וֹא אַתָּ֣ה מִקֶּ֗דֶם יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהַ֛י קְדֹשִׁ֖י לֹ֣א נָמ֑וּת יְהוָה֙ לְמִשְׁפָּ֣ט שַׂמְתּ֔וֹ וְצ֖וּר לְהוֹכִ֥יחַ יְסַדְתּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Are not you from antiquity, Yahweh my God, my Holy One? We will not die. Yahweh, for judgment you have appointed it, and Rock, to reprove you have established it.

en.L: Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} not from of old, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} my God, my Holy One? We will not die. \q {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have appointed it for judgment; \q and, Rock, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have established it to reprove.
en.B: Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} not from everlasting, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, my God, my Holy One? We will not die. \q {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have appointed them to execute judgment; \q Rock, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have set them in place to bring correction.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have existed from the very beginning. You are my God, my holy God. We will not die. \q {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have chosen the Babylonians to carry out {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} judgment. \q You are our Rock, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have sent them to correct us.

fr.L: N’es-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pas dès les temps anciens, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} mon Dieu, mon Saint ? Nous ne mourrons pas. \q {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} l’as établie pour le jugement ; \q et, Rocher, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} l’as fondée pour corriger.
fr.B: N’es-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pas depuis toujours, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, mon Dieu, mon Saint ? Nous ne mourrons pas. \q {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} les as chargés d’exécuter le jugement ; \q Rocher, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} les as placés là pour corriger.
fr.R: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} existes depuis le tout début. Tu es mon Dieu, mon Dieu saint. Nous ne mourrons pas. \q {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as choisi les Babyloniens pour exécuter {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} jugement. \q Tu es notre Rocher, et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} les as envoyés pour nous corriger.

es.L: ¿No [eres] {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} desde la antigüedad, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, Dios mío, Santo mío? No moriremos. \q {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, para juicio lo has puesto; \q y, Roca, para corregir lo has establecido.
es.B: ¿No eres {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} desde siempre, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, mi Dios, mi Santo? No moriremos. \q {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} los has puesto para ejecutar juicio; \q oh Roca, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} los has establecido para corregir.
es.R: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} existes desde el principio. Eres mi Dios, mi Dios santo. No moriremos. \q {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} escogiste a los babilonios para llevar a cabo {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} juicio. \q Eres nuestra Roca, y {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} los has enviado para corregirnos.

sw.L: Je, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} si wa tangu zamani, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wangu, Mtakatifu wangu? Hatutakufa. \q Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, umeliweka kwa ajili ya hukumu; \q na, Ee Mwamba, umeliimarisha ili kuonya.
sw.B: Je, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} si wa tangu milele, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wangu, Mtakatifu wangu? Hatutakufa. \q Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, umewaweka ili watekeleze hukumu; \q Ee Mwamba, umewasimika ili walete marudi.
sw.R: Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} umekuwepo tangu mwanzo kabisa. Wewe ni Mungu wangu, Mungu wangu mtakatifu. Hatutakufa. \q Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, umewachagua Wababeli ili walete hukumu {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}. \q Wewe ni Mwamba wetu, {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}} umewatuma ili watuadhibu tupate kujirekebisha.

vi.L: Chẳng phải {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} có từ thuở xưa sao, lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của con, Đấng Thánh của con? Chúng con sẽ không chết. \q Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã lập nó để thi hành sự phán xét; \q và, hỡi Vầng Đá, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã đặt nó để quở phạt.
vi.B: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của con, Đấng Thánh của con, chẳng phải {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hằng có từ đời đời sao? Chúng con sẽ không chết. \q Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã chỉ định chúng để thi hành sự phán xét; \q lạy Vầng Đá, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã lập chúng lên để sửa phạt.
vi.R: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã có từ ban đầu. Ngài là Đức Chúa Trời của con, là Đức Chúa Trời thánh khiết của con. Chúng con sẽ không chết. \q Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã chọn người Ba-by-lôn để thi hành sự phán xét của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \q Ngài là Vầng Đá của chúng con, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã sai chúng đến để sửa phạt chúng con.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 나의 하나님, 나의 거룩하신 분이시여, 주님께서는 옛적부터 계시지 않습니까? 저희는 죽지 않을 것입니다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 주님께서 심판하시려고 그것을 세우셨습니다. \q 반석이시여, 주님께서 꾸짖으시려고 그것을 두셨습니다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 나의 하나님, 나의 거룩하신 분이시여, 주님께서는 영원 전부터 계신 분이 아니십니까? 저희는 죽지 않을 것입니다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 주님께서 심판을 행하시려고 그들을 세우셨습니다. \q 반석이시여, 주님께서 바로잡으시려고 그들을 두셨습니다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 주님께서는 맨 처음부터 계셨습니다. 주님은 저의 하나님, 저의 거룩하신 하나님이십니다. 저희는 죽지 않을 것입니다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 주님께서 바빌로니아 사람들을 택하셔서 주님의 심판을 행하게 하셨습니다. \q 주님은 저희의 반석이십니다. 주님께서 저희를 바로잡으시려고 그들을 보내셨습니다.

pt.L: Não és {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} desde a antiguidade, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, meu Deus, meu Santo? Não morreremos. \q {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} a puseste para o juízo; \q e, ó Rocha, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} a estabeleceste para repreender.
pt.B: Não és {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} desde a eternidade, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, meu Deus, meu Santo? Não morreremos. \q {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} os designaste para executar o juízo; \q ó Rocha, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} os estabeleceste para trazer correção.
pt.R: {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} existes desde o princípio de tudo. Tu és o meu Deus, o meu Deus santo. Não vamos morrer. \q {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} escolheste os babilônios para executar o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} juízo. \q Tu és a nossa Rocha, e {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} os enviaste para nos corrigir.

decisions.choice: the prophet's second complaint begins
decisions.reason: Habakkuk answers the LORD's words with a confession of faith and a new complaint. He begins with what he knows: the LORD is eternal, his own God and the Holy One. He ends with the question of verse 13: how can such a God use the Babylonians?

decisions.choice: We will not die
alternatives: You do not die (said of God, by scribal tradition)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "we will not die": the people trust that the eternal God will not let them be wiped out. Jewish scribal tradition lists this verse among a few places where the scribes are said to have changed the wording out of reverence, so that an original "You do not die", said of God, became "we will not die". The translation follows the text as it stands.

decisions.choice: appointed it for judgment ... to reprove: the Babylonians as the LORD's instrument
alternatives: to judge and correct the nations
decisions.reason: "It" is the Babylonian nation. The prophet accepts that the LORD has appointed it to judge and to correct, most likely Judah (verse 4), as the LORD said in verse 6. "Rock" is a title of God as the firm, safe refuge of his people (Deuteronomy 32:4; Psalm 18:3).

decisions.choice: them (B); the Babylonians, to correct us, our Rock (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "them" for the singular "it", the Babylonian nation; Readable names them and says whom they correct (m3). "Rock" keeps its capital as a title of God.

decisions.choice: "lo has puesto", "lo has establecido"
decisions.reason: At L the object "lo" keeps the Hebrew singular "it" (the nation); B and R say "them", as the English does.

decisions.choice: "Ee Mwamba" (L, B); "Mwamba wetu" (R)
decisions.reason: Rock is a title of God here, so it is capitalized as in the published Psalms; Readable makes it "our Rock", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "my Holy One" is "나의 거룩하신 분" (L, B) and "저의 거룩하신 하나님" (R); "Rock" as a title is "반석" with the vocative "반석이시여"
decisions.reason: Habakkuk speaks to God, so the title takes -시- (the term sheet keeps "거룩한 이" for God's own mouth). In the vocative cluster "나의" is the fixed address of the psalms; Readable turns it into a sentence in 합쇼체 with "저의".

decisions.choice: "Vầng Đá", capitalised, for God as Rock
decisions.reason: As the published Psalms address God; the capital marks it as a name for God, as the English "Rock".

source.text: טְה֤וֹר עֵינַ֨יִם֙ מֵרְא֣וֹת רָ֔ע וְהַבִּ֥יט אֶל־עָמָ֖ל לֹ֣א תוּכָ֑ל לָ֤מָּה תַבִּיט֙ בּֽוֹגְדִ֔ים תַּחֲרִ֕ישׁ בְּבַלַּ֥ע רָשָׁ֖ע צַדִּ֥יק מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: [You are too] pure of eyes for seeing evil, and to look at trouble you are not able. Why do you look at [those who] act treacherously, [why] are you silent when swallows up a wicked [person] a righteous [person] more than him?

en.L: [You are too] pure of eyes to see evil, \q and to look on wrongdoing {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are not able. \q Why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} look on those who deal treacherously, \q [why] are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} silent when [the] wicked swallows up [one] more righteous than himself?
en.B: Your eyes are too pure to look on evil, \q and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} cannot look on wrongdoing. \q Why then do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} look on the treacherous, \q and keep silent while the wicked swallow up those more righteous than they?
en.R: Your eyes are so pure that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} cannot stand to look at evil. \q You cannot put up with wrongdoing. \q So why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} put up with these treacherous people? \q Why are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} silent while wicked people destroy those who are better than they are?

fr.L: [Tu as les] yeux trop purs pour voir le mal, \q et regarder la peine, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ne [le] peux pas. \q Pourquoi regardes-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ceux qui agissent avec perfidie, \q [pourquoi] {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} tais-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} quand le méchant engloutit [celui qui est] plus juste que lui ?
fr.B: Tes yeux sont trop purs pour voir le mal, \q et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ne peux pas regarder l’injustice. \q Pourquoi donc regardes-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} les traîtres, \q et gardes-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} le silence quand le méchant engloutit plus juste que lui ?
fr.R: Tes yeux sont si purs que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ne supportes pas de voir le mal. \q Tu ne peux pas tolérer l’injustice. \q Alors pourquoi supportes-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ces traîtres ? \q Pourquoi restes-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} silencieux quand des méchants détruisent des gens meilleurs qu’eux ?

es.L: [Eres demasiado] puro de ojos para ver el mal, \q y mirar la opresión no puedes. \q ¿Por qué miras a los que actúan con traición, \q [por qué] callas cuando el impío se traga al que es más justo que él?
es.B: Tus ojos son demasiado puros para mirar el mal, \q y {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} no puedes contemplar la opresión. \q ¿Por qué, entonces, toleras a los traidores, \q y callas mientras los malvados se tragan a los que son más justos que ellos?
es.R: Tus ojos son tan puros que no soportas ver el mal. \q No puedes tolerar la injusticia. \q Entonces, ¿por qué toleras a esta gente traicionera? \q ¿Por qué callas mientras los malvados destruyen a los que son mejores que ellos?

sw.L: [Wewe una] macho safi mno kuona uovu, \q wala huwezi kutazama udhalimu. \q Kwa nini unawatazama wasaliti, \q [kwa nini] unanyamaza mwovu anapommeza [mtu] mwenye haki kuliko yeye?
sw.B: Macho {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} ni safi mno kuweza kutazama uovu, \q wala huwezi kuvumilia kutazama udhalimu. \q Basi kwa nini unawatazama wasaliti, \q na kunyamaza waovu wanapowameza walio wenye haki kuliko wao?
sw.R: Macho {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} ni safi sana, hivi kwamba huwezi kuvumilia kutazama uovu. \q Huwezi kuvumilia udhalimu. \q Basi kwa nini unawavumilia watu hawa wasaliti? \q Kwa nini unanyamaza waovu wanapowaangamiza watu walio bora kuliko wao?

vi.L: [Mắt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}] quá tinh sạch để nhìn điều ác, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không thể nhìn xem điều sai trái. \q Tại sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nhìn những kẻ phản bội, \q [tại sao] {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} im lặng khi kẻ ác nuốt [người] công chính hơn nó?
vi.B: Mắt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} quá thánh sạch nên không thể nhìn điều ác, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không thể nhìn xem điều sai trái. \q Vậy sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lại nhìn những kẻ bội tín, \q và cứ im lặng khi kẻ ác nuốt chửng người công chính hơn chúng?
vi.R: Mắt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} tinh sạch đến nỗi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không chịu nổi khi nhìn điều ác. \q Ngài không thể dung túng điều sai trái. \q Vậy tại sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lại dung túng những kẻ phản bội này? \q Tại sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} im lặng khi kẻ gian ác tiêu diệt những người tốt hơn chúng?

ko.L: [주님께서는] 눈이 정결하셔서 악을 보지 못하시고, \q 고통을 바라보실 수 없습니다. \q 어찌하여 배신하는 자들을 바라보시며, \q 악인이 자기보다 의로운 자를 삼킬 때에 [어찌하여] 잠잠하십니까?
ko.B: 주님은 눈이 너무 맑으셔서 악을 보지 못하시고, \q 악한 일을 그냥 보고 계실 수 없는 분입니다. \q 그런데 어찌하여 배신하는 자들을 보고만 계십니까? \q 악인이 자기보다 의로운 사람을 삼키는데 어찌하여 잠잠히 계십니까?
ko.R: 주님의 눈은 너무 깨끗하셔서 악한 것을 차마 보지 못하십니다. \q 주님은 나쁜 일을 참지 못하시는 분입니다. \q 그런데 왜 이 믿을 수 없는 자들을 그냥 두십니까? \q 악한 사람들이 자기들보다 나은 사람들을 망하게 하는데, 왜 아무 말씀도 하지 않으십니까?

pt.L: [Tu és] puro de olhos [demais] para ver o mal, \q e olhar para a aflição {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} não podes. \q Por que olhas para os que agem traiçoeiramente, \q [por que] {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} calas quando o ímpio engole [aquele que é] mais justo que ele?
pt.B: Os {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} olhos são puros demais para olhar o mal, \q e {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} não podes contemplar a opressão. \q Por que, então, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} olhas para os traiçoeiros \q e ficas calado enquanto os ímpios engolem os que são mais justos que eles?
pt.R: Os {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} olhos são tão puros que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} não suportas olhar o mal. \q Tu não toleras a maldade. \q Então por que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} toleras essa gente traiçoeira? \q Por que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ficas calado enquanto os maus destroem os que são melhores do que eles?

decisions.choice: too pure to look on evil, yet God seems to look on: Habakkuk's problem
decisions.reason: "Look on" means to tolerate or approve. Habakkuk sets what he believes about God's holiness beside what he sees: the LORD cannot approve evil, yet he lets the treacherous Babylonians prosper. The question is not answered until chapter 2.

decisions.choice: the treacherous: those who break faith
decisions.reason: The word is used of those who betray trust, break agreements and deal deceitfully (Isaiah 21:2; 24:16). Here it describes the Babylonians.

decisions.choice: the wicked swallows up one more righteous than himself
decisions.reason: The wicked is the Babylonian; the one "more righteous" is Judah, or the righteous within it. Habakkuk does not say that Judah is innocent (verses 2-4), only that it is not as wicked as the people sent to punish it.

decisions.choice: the wicked, those more righteous than they (B); wicked people, those who are better (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use plurals for the Hebrew singulars, which stand for whole groups, so that no gender span is needed.

source.text: וַתַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה אָדָ֖ם כִּדְגֵ֣י הַיָּ֑ם כְּרֶ֖מֶשׂ לֹא־מֹשֵׁ֥ל בּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And you have made humankind like the fish of the sea, like creeping things [that have] not a ruler over it.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made humankind like the fish of the sea, \q like creeping things [with] no ruler over them.
en.B: You have made people like fish in the sea, \q like creatures that crawl, with no ruler over them.
en.R: You have made people like fish in the sea, \q like little sea creatures that have no leader to protect them.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as fait l’humanité comme les poissons de la mer, \q comme les bêtes qui rampent, [qui n’ont] pas de maître sur elles.
fr.B: Tu as rendu les humains semblables aux poissons de la mer, \q aux bêtes qui rampent et n’ont pas de chef.
fr.R: Tu as rendu les gens pareils aux poissons de la mer, \q aux petites bêtes marines qui n’ont pas de chef pour les protéger.

es.L: Y has hecho a los seres humanos como los peces del mar, \q como los reptiles [que] no tienen quien los gobierne.
es.B: Has hecho a la gente como los peces del mar, \q como los animales que se arrastran, sin nadie que los gobierne.
es.R: Has hecho a la gente como los peces del mar, \q como pequeños animales marinos que no tienen un jefe que los proteja.

sw.L: Nawe umewafanya wanadamu kama samaki wa baharini, \q kama viumbe vitambaavyo visivyo na mtawala juu yao.
sw.B: Umewafanya watu kama samaki baharini, \q kama viumbe vitambaavyo visivyo na mtawala.
sw.R: Umewafanya watu kama samaki baharini, \q kama viumbe vidogo vya baharini visivyo na kiongozi wa kuvilinda.

vi.L: Ngài đã làm cho loài người như cá dưới biển, \q như loài bò sát không [có] ai cai trị chúng.
vi.B: Ngài đã làm cho con người như cá dưới biển, \q như loài bò sát chẳng có ai cai quản.
vi.R: Ngài đã làm cho con người giống như cá dưới biển, \q như những sinh vật nhỏ bé không có ai che chở.

ko.L: 주님께서 사람을 바다의 물고기처럼, \q 그 위에 다스리는 자가 없는 기어 다니는 것들처럼 만드셨습니다.
ko.B: 주님께서 사람들을 바다의 물고기처럼, \q 다스리는 자도 없는 기어 다니는 생물처럼 만드셨습니다.
ko.R: 주님께서 사람들을 바닷속 물고기처럼 만드셨습니다. \q 지켜 줄 우두머리가 없는 작은 바다 생물처럼 만드셨습니다.

pt.L: E {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} fizeste a humanidade como os peixes do mar, \q como os répteis [que] não têm quem os governe.
pt.B: Fizeste as pessoas como peixes no mar, \q como criaturas que rastejam, sem ninguém que as governe.
pt.R: Fizeste as pessoas como peixes no mar, \q como pequenos bichos do mar que não têm um líder para protegê-los.

decisions.choice: humankind like fish and creeping things: creation turned upside down
decisions.reason: In Genesis 1:26-28 humankind is made to rule over the fish of the sea and every creeping thing. Now, Habakkuk complains, God has let people be treated like fish themselves, with no ruler to protect them, as the next verses show.

decisions.choice: creeping things: small creatures that move about
decisions.reason: The word is used of small creatures on land and of the creatures of the sea (Psalm 104:25), which fits the fish of the first line.

decisions.choice: no leader to protect them
decisions.reason: Readable adds "to protect them" to say why having no ruler matters here.

source.text: כֻּלֹּה֙ בְּחַכָּ֣ה הֵֽעֲלָ֔ה יְגֹרֵ֣הוּ בְחֶרְמ֔וֹ וְיַאַסְפֵ֖הוּ בְּמִכְמַרְתּ֑וֹ עַל־כֵּ֖ן יִשְׂמַ֥ח וְיָגִֽיל׃

records.literal_gloss: All of it with a hook he brings up; he drags it away in his net, and he gathers it in his dragnet; therefore he rejoices and is glad.

en.L: All of it he brings up with a hook; \q he drags it away in his net \q and gathers it in his dragnet; \q therefore he rejoices and is glad.
en.B: The enemy pulls them all up with a hook; \q he drags them away in his net \q and gathers them in his fishing net; \q so he rejoices and celebrates.
en.R: The Babylonians catch people with hooks. \q They drag them away in nets \q and gather them up in fishing nets. \q Then they celebrate and are happy.

fr.L: Tout entière il la fait monter à l’hameçon ; \q il la traîne dans son filet \q et la rassemble dans sa senne ; \q c’est pourquoi il se réjouit et exulte.
fr.B: L’ennemi les tire tous à l’hameçon ; \q il les entraîne dans son filet \q et les ramasse dans sa senne ; \q alors il se réjouit et jubile.
fr.R: Les Babyloniens attrapent les gens avec des hameçons. \q Ils les traînent dans des filets \q et les ramassent dans des filets de pêche. \q Puis ils font la fête, tout heureux.

es.L: A todos los saca con anzuelo; \q los arrastra en su red \q y los recoge en su red barredera; \q por tanto, se alegra y se regocija.
es.B: El enemigo los saca a todos con anzuelo; \q los arrastra en su red \q y los recoge en su red de pesca; \q por eso se alegra y hace fiesta.
es.R: Los babilonios atrapan a la gente con anzuelos. \q La arrastran en sus redes \q y la recogen en sus redes de pesca. \q Luego celebran llenos de alegría.

sw.L: Wote anawavua kwa ndoano; \q anawakokota kwa wavu wake \q na kuwakusanya katika jarife lake; \q kwa hiyo anafurahi na kushangilia.
